The displayed formulae of an organic compound is shown below.

![4-1-q1-igcse-chemistry-mcq](assets/001-4-1-q1-igcse-chemistry-mcq.png)

What is the empirical formula of this compound?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is B**

- Empirical formula is the simplest ratio of atoms of each element
- The molecular formula for this compound is C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>Br<sub>2</sub>
- Therefore the simplest ratio of each atom is CH<sub>2</sub>Br

parts.problem_md:
Ethene (C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>) can be converted into chloroethene (C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>3</sub>Cl) in a two-stage process.

The first stage is to convert ethene into 1,2-dichloroethane, C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>Cl<sub>2</sub>

Ethene is reacted with hydrogen chloride and oxygen.

Complete the chemical equation for this reaction.

.......... C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub> + .......... HCl + .......... O<sub>2</sub> → .......... C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>Cl<sub>2</sub> + .......... H<sub>2</sub>O
parts.solution_md:
The completed chemical equation for this reaction is:

- 2C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub> + 4HCl + O<sub>2</sub> → 2C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>Cl<sub>2</sub> + 2H<sub>2</sub>O; **[1 mark] **
*Multiples and fractions are accepted*

**[Total: 1 mark]**

- *Remember: **You can put a big number in front of the chemical to say how many of that chemical there are, but you cannot add small numbers to the chemicals *

  - *e.g. 2C*<sub>*2*</sub>*H*<sub>*4*</sub>* means that you have 2 x C*<sub>*2*</sub>*H*<sub>*4*</sub>* molecules*
  - *e.g. changing HCl to H*<sub>*2*</sub>*Cl*<sub>*2*</sub>* might help with balancing the equation but it has changed the chemical*
- *One possible way to balance this equation is:*

  - *Double the HCl to balance the chlorine atoms on either side, which actually balances the carbons and hydrogens as well C*<sub>*2*</sub>*H*<sub>*4*</sub>* + **2**HCl + .......... O*<sub>*2*</sub>* → C*<sub>*2*</sub>*H*<sub>*4*</sub>*Cl*<sub>*2*</sub>* + .......... H*<sub>*2*</sub>*O*
  - *You can balance the one oxygen on the right-hand side by using half an oxygen molecule C*<sub>*2*</sub>*H*<sub>*4*</sub>* + 2HCl + **½**O*<sub>*2*</sub>* → C*<sub>*2*</sub>*H*<sub>*4*</sub>*Cl*<sub>*2*</sub>* + H*<sub>*2*</sub>*O*
  - *This can be doubled to work with whole numbers 2C*<sub>*2*</sub>*H*<sub>*4*</sub>* + 4HCl + O*<sub>*2*</sub>* → 2C*<sub>*2*</sub>*H*<sub>*4*</sub>*Cl*<sub>*2*</sub>* + 2H*<sub>*2*</sub>*O*
- *Find a way that you are comfortable to balance equations, even if you take the time to draw the molecules out*

  - *These can be easy marks to pick up in your exam once you are confident with this skill*

parts.problem_md:
In the second stage, 1,2-dichloroethane is converted into chloroethene.

C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>Cl<sub>2</sub> → C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>3</sub>Cl + HCl

This is a thermal decomposition reaction.

State what is meant by the term **thermal decomposition.**
parts.solution_md:
Thermal decomposition is:

- Breaking down (a chemical / compound) by heating / using heat; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 1 mark]**

- *Thermal links to heat*
- *Decomposition links to breaking down*
- *Therefore, thermal decomposition is using heat to break **something** a chemical down*

  - *Try and avoid words like "something" and be specific with keywords as this could cost you a mark in an exam*
  - *If you are not sure if a chemical is ionic, covalent or metallic then you can just use "a chemical" and you don't unnecessarily lose a mark *

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows the displayed formula of chloroethene.

![chloroethene-edexcel-2019ju1c](assets/002-chloroethene-edexcel-2019ju1c.png)

i) State why chloroethene is described as an unsaturated compound.

(1)

ii) Describe a test to show that chloroethene is unsaturated.

(2)
parts.solution_md:
i) Chloroethene is described as an unsaturated compound because:

- It contains a (carbon-carbon) double bond; **[1 mark] **

ii) A test to show that chloroethene is unsaturated is:

Any **one **of the following pairs:

Pair 1:

- Add bromine water / solution 
**OR**
** **Add Br<sub>2</sub> (aq); **[1 mark]**
- (The bromine water) is decolourised 
**OR**
** **The bromine water changes (from orange / yellow / brown) to colourless; **[1 mark]**

Pair 2:

- Add acidified potassium manganate(VII) solution
 **OR **
Add KMnO<sub>4</sub> (aq);** [1 mark]**
- (The acidified potassium manganate(VII) solution) is decolourised 
**OR**
** **(The acidified potassium manganate(VII) solution) changes (from purple) to colourless; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 3 marks]**

- *Saturated compounds contain carbon-carbon single bonds*
- *Unsaturated compounds contain at least one carbon=carbon double (or multiple) bond*
- *The test for an unsaturated compound is that bromine water decolourises *

  - *This is because the bromine is reacted out of the bromine water, which leaves just colourless water *

parts.problem_md: Name the polymer formed from chloroethene.
parts.solution_md:
The polymer formed from chloroethene is:

- Poly(chloroethene) / polychloroethene 
**OR **
Polyvinyl chloride / PVC; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 1 mark]**

- *To name a polymer from its monomer, you simply put poly in front of the name*

  - *Ethene → polyethene*
  - *Propene → polypropene*

parts.problem_md: Which of the following is **not** a feature of a homologous series?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is B**

- The statement that is **not **a feature of a homologous series is: B / Compounds have the same physical properties
- Compounds in the same homologous series demonstrate a graduation in their physical properties
- This means there are small differences in physical properties, this happens as the size of the organic molecule increases

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: Compounds have the same functional group

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: Compounds have the same physical properties

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: Compounds have the same general formula

parts.problem_md: Which of the following reactions is an example of an addition reaction?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is B**

- The example of an addition reaction is: **B** / C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub> + Br<sub>2</sub> → C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>Br<sub>2</sub>

- An addition reaction takes place when two or more molecules combine to form a larger molecule with no other product
- Alkenes undergo addition reactions with hydrogen, the halogens and water
- In this case, ethene reacts with bromine to form dibromoethane
- **A** is incorrect as this equation shows incomplete combustion
- **C** is incorrect as this equation shows complete combustion
- **D** is incorrect as this equation shows a substitution reaction
